text: [scripted dry run, regenerate with a live key: decisions are scripted, tool outputs are real] Plan: check image quality and CBC coherence for both samples, infer geometry, sweep channel widths over the observed MCD range, isolate the high-sphericity subpopulation, then design a falsifiable microfluidic test.

output.note: Diameters in pixels; only ratios are used (the CBC fixes the absolute scale).

text: Image data usable: 300 cells kept in synthetic_healthy, 300 in synthetic_hs; 17% of synthetic_hs cells show almost no central pallor. Next, CBC coherence.

checks.note: Approximation V∝D³; smear artefacts widen the image CV.
Approximation V∝D³; smear artefacts widen the image CV.

text: synthetic_hs: RDW_vs_diameter_CV is INCOHERENT (CBC RDW-CV 17.5% vs 9.76% implied by the image). I continue: volumes are anchored on the MCV, not on the RDW, so the geometry stays usable, but the smear may under-represent the size spread; the flag goes into the report. Now geometry.

synthetic_healthy has SI p90 0.772 and 1% of cells above SI 0.8, against 39% in synthetic_hs: I isolate SI > 0.8 as the subpopulation threshold (HYPOTHESIS). MCD spans 2.85 to 4.23 µm, so I sweep 2.5-4.5 µm rather than the default range.

output.legend: fractions of cells; passes = no membrane stretch needed

text: The pass curves differ most at 3.12 µm (88% of synthetic_healthy vs 44% of synthetic_hs pass without stretch); I use this width for the borderline cell. Picking cells for the 3D view.

output.reason: closest to the sample median volume and sphericity
largest minimum cylindrical diameter (least surface reserve)
minimum cylindrical diameter closest to the 3.12 µm channel

text: Worst cell c275 has MCD 4.23 µm. I check it at 3.12 µm with a 2x stiffness HYPOTHESIS to show the geometric verdict does not depend on stiffness, then design the experiment.

output.hypothesis: At 3.12 µm, synthetic_healthy passes at 87% vs synthetic_hs at 43%, driven by surface-to-volume ratio alone.
output.falsified_if: Measured pass fractions do not differ, or the difference disappears after osmotic swelling/shrinking controls.
caveats: Model assumes cylindrical channels; rectangular microfluidic channels need an equivalent-diameter correction.
Stiffness is not modelled; rigid cells may fail where geometry allows passage.

report.title: synthetic_hs shows a spherical subpopulation that fails 3.12 µm channels
report.summary: synthetic_hs contains a high-sphericity subpopulation (39% of cells) whose surface-to-volume ratio is too low to pass narrow channels; this is compatible with a spherocytic phenotype, to be confirmed. Proposed test: constrictions at 2.87, 3.12, 3.37 µm with 18 cells per sample.

findings.text: 39% of cells in synthetic_hs have a sphericity index above 0.8 (INFERRED SI; threshold is a HYPOTHESIS), versus 1% in synthetic_healthy.

This subpopulation has a median minimum cylindrical diameter of 3.53 µm versus 3.03 µm for the rest of synthetic_hs (COMPUTED): with less surface for its volume it cannot fold into a 3 µm capsule; 97% of it is BLOCKED at 3 µm.

D50 (width where half the cells pass without stretch) is 3.16 µm for synthetic_hs versus 2.99 µm for synthetic_healthy (COMPUTED). At 3.12 µm the model predicts 87% passage for synthetic_healthy and 43% for synthetic_hs.
Worst cell c275 is BLOCKED at 3.12 µm: it would need 22% area strain, beyond the 3% lysis limit (COMPUTED). A 2x stiffness (HYPOTHESIS) cannot change a geometric BLOCKED verdict.
CBC flag for synthetic_hs: RDW-CV 17.5% (CONSTRAINED) vs 9.76% implied by the image diameters (MEASURED): the smear may under-represent the size spread; to be confirmed on another field.

consistency_flags.note: Approximation V∝D³; smear artefacts widen the image CV.

experiment.hypothesis: At 3.12 µm, synthetic_healthy passes at 87% vs synthetic_hs at 43%, driven by surface-to-volume ratio alone.
experiment.falsified_if: Measured pass fractions do not differ, or the difference disappears after osmotic swelling/shrinking controls.
caveats: Model assumes cylindrical channels; rectangular microfluidic channels need an equivalent-diameter correction.
Stiffness is not modelled; rigid cells may fail where geometry allows passage.

limitations: Sphericity is inferred from central pallor (linear map: pallor ratio 0.4 gives SI 0.74, no pallor gives SI 0.92); validated only on annotated data.
No mechanical simulation: capsule model in rigid cylindrical channels; stiffness is never predicted from images.
Synthetic samples and demo CBC values, not patient data.
